title: Model consecutive integers with a quadratic equation

source_reference.notes: Original Edexcel 4MA1 Higher-style item for the Year 10 quadratics MVP. Edexcel pivot metadata applied.

problem_text: The product of two consecutive positive integers is 72. Let the smaller integer be x. Form an equation and find the two integers.
student_prompt: Show the equation in x and solve it.

error_category_mapping.diagnostic_sentence: Consecutive integers differ by 1, so the next integer is x + 1, not x + 2.
The question asks for positive integers, so reject the negative solution.

hint_ladder.title: What does consecutive mean?
hint_ladder.prompt: Consecutive positive integers differ by one. Represent the second integer in terms of the first before forming the product.

hint_ladder.title: Pick a starting move
hint_ladder.prompt: Use the product statement to form an equation, then rearrange it into standard quadratic form.

hint_ladder.title: A common slip
hint_ladder.prompt: Many students find two algebraic solutions but forget the word positive. The context decides which solution is acceptable.

hint_ladder.title: The general pattern
hint_ladder.prompt: For consecutive integer problems, define the smaller value, express the next one as one more, form the product equation, solve, and interpret. Apply this pattern; do not copy an example.

common_errors: adds the integers instead of multiplying
expected_solution_steps.diagnostic_sentence: The stuck point is representing consecutive integers.
The stuck point is rearranging the product equation.

expected_solution_steps.expression: x = 8, so the integers are 8 and 9
expected_solution_steps.diagnostic_sentence: The stuck point is interpreting the solution in the context.

mark_scheme_notes: Award marks for model, rearrangement, factorisation, and contextual integer pair.
examiner_report_notes: Likely errors: wrong consecutive representation and failure to interpret root.
metacognition_prompt: Before you start, what has to be defined before you can form the equation?
